title: Arunachal permits, seasons and altitude
meta_description: Arunachal practical guide: Inner Line Permit and Protected Area Permit basics, the best month for each circuit, monsoon roads, Sela altitude and what to pack.
summary: Indians need an Inner Line Permit and foreigners a Protected Area Permit to enter Arunachal; list every district you will visit. October–November and March–April are the best months, December–February brings snow at Sela and Tawang, and June–August is monsoon. Sela Pass is about 4,170 m, so acclimatise in Dirang first.

sections.heading: Inner Line Permit for Indian travellers
paras: Arunachal Pradesh is protected by the Inner Line system, which dates from colonial-era regulations and is still in force. Indian citizens from outside the state need an Inner Line Permit, or ILP, to enter. As we understand the current process, tourists apply online for an e-ILP on the Arunachal Pradesh government's official portal, upload a photo and an identity document, pay a fee of a few hundred rupees, and download the permit to print.

The permit names the districts you may visit, so list every one on your route: West Kameng and Tawang for the Tawang circuit; Papum Pare and Lower Subansiri for Ziro; East Siang, West Siang and Shi Yomi for Pasighat and Mechuka; Lower Dibang Valley for Roing; Changlang for Namdapha. Permits are checked at entry gates such as Bhalukpong, Banderdewa, Ruksin and Jagun, and sometimes inside the state. Carry two printouts and the original ID you used. Rules, fees and validity periods change, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Protected Area Permit for foreign nationals
paras: Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit, or PAP. As we understand it, this is usually arranged through a registered Indian tour operator, who applies on your behalf with passport and visa copies and pays the fee. The permit is typically valid for about 30 days and covers named circuits or districts. Rules on minimum group size have been relaxed in recent years for some circuits, but they can change, and citizens of a few countries face extra restrictions or cannot get a PAP at all.

Apply at least two to three weeks before you travel, carry several copies with your passport, and keep to the areas named on the permit. Some border points, such as Bum La above Tawang, need separate permission even for permit holders. Check current status before you travel.
list: Indian visitors: e-ILP, applied online, a few hundred rupees
Foreign visitors: PAP through a registered operator, fee per person
Both: list every district; carry printouts and original ID
Border points and some sanctuaries: extra permission needed

sections.heading: Month by month: when each circuit works
paras: Arunachal's weather is shaped by the monsoon and by altitude. The plains-edge towns of Bhalukpong, Pasighat and Roing are hot and very wet in summer, while Tawang and the passes are cold and snowy in winter. The table shows how we rate each circuit by season.

sections.heading: The monsoon and road closures
paras: From June to September, the southwest monsoon brings some of the heaviest rain in India to the foothills of Arunachal. Landslides close roads for hours or days, especially on the Bomdila–Tawang highway, the Aalo–Mechuka road and around Ziro, and rivers can wash out bridges. Flights are delayed by cloud. We do not plan first trips in these months.

If you must travel then, keep plans loose, build in two spare days, and ask your driver or homestay host each evening about the next day's road. Leeches are common in forests and on walks below about 2,500 m. Pack light rain gear and quick-drying clothes. In every season, road works and occasional closures happen, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Altitude on the Tawang road
paras: Most of Arunachal that travellers visit is below 2,000 m: Ziro, Dirang, Mechuka, Pasighat and Roing are all comfortable for healthy people. The exception is the Tawang circuit. Bomdila is about 2,400 m and Tawang town about 2,670 m, with the monastery near 3,000 m. Sela Pass is about 4,170 m, and the high lakes beyond Tawang are above 4,000 m.

Most people feel only mild breathlessness, but headaches, nausea and poor sleep are possible, especially if you climb fast from the plains. The simplest protection is time: sleep a night or two in Dirang at about 1,600 m before crossing Sela, keep stops at the pass short, drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol on your first night in Tawang. If symptoms get worse rather than better, go down. Children, older travellers and anyone with heart or lung conditions should talk to their doctor before the trip; we make no medical promises.

sections.heading: What to pack for Arunachal
paras: Packing depends on the circuit and season, but a few items are useful on almost every trip. Arunachal has long roads, simple rooms, patchy power and changeable weather, so prepare for all of them.
list: Printouts of your ILP or PAP and the original ID used to apply
Warm layers: thermals, fleece and a down jacket for Tawang from October to April
A light rain jacket in every month
Leech socks for Namdapha, Talle Valley and forest walks
Motion-sickness remedies and snacks for long Sumo days
A headtorch and power bank for power cuts
Enough cash for several days; ATMs are few outside district towns
A refillable bottle and purification tablets

faqs.q: How do I apply for an Inner Line Permit for Arunachal?
faqs.a: Apply online on the Arunachal Pradesh government's official e-ILP portal with a photo and ID, list every district you will visit, pay the fee and print the permit. Approval is usually quick. Rules and fees change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which districts should I list on my ILP for Tawang?
faqs.a: West Kameng, which covers Bhalukpong, Bomdila, Dirang and Sela, and Tawang district. If you plan to go on to Ziro, add Papum Pare and Lower Subansiri. Check current status before you travel.

Yes, with a Protected Area Permit arranged through a registered tour operator. Some border areas need extra permission. Citizens of a few countries face restrictions. Check current status before you travel and apply two to three weeks ahead.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate permit for Bum La?
faqs.a: Yes. Bum La on the border above Tawang needs extra permission from the authorities in Tawang, and access is not always allowed. Ask your hotel or driver to help on arrival.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Arunachal?
faqs.a: October and November for most circuits, followed by March and April. December to February suits snow lovers in Tawang and Mayudia, and the dry season in Namdapha. June to August is monsoon, with frequent landslides.

faqs.q: Is Sela Pass open in winter?
faqs.a: The Sela Tunnel, opened in 2024, keeps the Tawang road open through most winter weather. The old road over the pass may close after heavy snow. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I avoid altitude sickness on the Tawang trip?
faqs.a: Sleep at least one night, ideally two, in Dirang before crossing Sela, drink plenty of water, keep the stop at the pass short and avoid alcohol on the first night in Tawang. Go down if symptoms worsen. Talk to your doctor if you have health conditions.

faqs.q: Is Arunachal open in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Yes, but heavy rain causes frequent landslides and road closures from June to September. If you travel then, add spare days and keep plans flexible.
At state entry gates such as Bhalukpong on the Tawang road, Banderdewa near Itanagar, Ruksin near Pasighat and Jagun on the Namdapha road, and sometimes at checkpoints inside the state.
